messages:
Noel (Hiring): Hey team  quick Q. I have a last-minute consulate appointment to get an urgent work visa for a customer trip next week. I paid the consular fee (USD 160) and paid USD 18 at a print shop for an expedited passport photocopy + form printing. Also travelling multi-city that day so wondering if I should claim per-diem for that travel day or just submit receipts. My manager Rafa is onsite with the client and may be slow to approve. Can we get an approval path?

Tessa (People Ops): Short: work-related visa/consular fees are reimbursable when travel is required by the company and there's a brief justification. Expedite printing/copies under USD 25 we treat as incidental reimbursable. For the travel day: choose receipts OR per-diem for that day, not both. If you have meal receipts, submit them; otherwise you can claim the daily per-diem.

Liam (Finance): Finance checklist: 1) upload the consulate receipt (showing fee and service), 2) upload the print shop receipt, 3) attach a short note explaining trip reason and dates, and 4) manager approval. If Rafa is slow, email finance-approvals@redwood.com with the Expensify link and CC people-ops; we can provisionally approve up to USD 500 for urgent travel expenses. VAT: not applicable for consular fees; print shop VAT reclaim depends on country invoice.

Rafa (Manager): Sorry Im at a client offsite. I approve the USD 160 consular fee and the USD 18 printing expense. Noel, please tag me in the expense and add: "client trip 2026-04-02 to 2026-04-05; consulate urgent". For the travel day, I prefer receipts—submit meal receipts if you have them.

Noel (Hiring): Thanks all  uploaded both receipts and added the trip note. Tagged Rafa and CCed finance-approvals in case approval lag is an issue.

Expense Bot: Reminder  submit within 30 days. Required uploads: consulate receipt, print shop receipt, manager approval (in-thread ok). Tag: "visa-fee" and category: Travel > Visa. Help: https://redwood.example/docs/expenses#visa-fees
